q: 1. According to the International Civil Aviation Organization (I.C.A.O.), the runway lengths of aerodromes, have been coded by ...........
explain: ICAO uses a code system (1-4) for length and letters (A-E) for wingspan/wheel span; textbooks often refer to the first five letters (A, B, C, D, E) for airport classification.

q: 2. *The minimum basic runway length of class ‘E’ type airport is
explain: Class E runways are for light aircraft and have a standard minimum length of 600m.

q: 3. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: air screw converts the energy given by the engine into speed
the propellers which are driven by turbine engines, are technically called turbo-props
the aircrafts which obtain the thrust directly from turbine engine, are called turbo-jets
the aircraft which is filled with a fan in front of turbo-jet engine, is called turbo-fan propelled aeroplane
explain: All listed statements correctly define the various types of aircraft propulsion systems.

q: 4. An aircraft is flying in an atmosphere of 30°C with a speed of 1260 km ph. Its speed is known as ...........
explain: The speed of sound at 30°C is approx 1260 km/h ($340.3 m/s \times 3.6 \approx 1225$). Matching the exact speed of sound makes it 'sonic'.

q: 5. *According to the International Civil Aviation Organization (I.C.A.O.) the runway lengths of aerodromes, have been coded by
explain: ICAO uses a numeric code (1-4) to categorize airports based on the runway's basic length.

options: sound varies 2.4 km p.h. per degree centigrade rise in temperature
sound at 0°C is called one mach
explain: These are standard approximations used in aeronautical engineering for the behavior of sound waves in air.

q: 7. *According to the International Civil Aviation Organization (I.C.A.O.). the strength of runway pavements, have been coded by
explain: Pavement strength is categorized using alphabetical codes (A-G) representing subgrade strength.

q: 8. *Stopping distance for aircraft during landing on runway should be,
explain: This formula relates velocity (V) and deceleration rate (d) to determine the necessary stopping distance.

q: 9. Speed of
options: sound varies 2.4 km p.h. Per degree centigrade rise in temperature
sound at 0°C is called one Mach
an aircraft flying at 2975 km p.h. is called 2.5 mach
explain: All these points accurately describe the behavior of sound speed and Mach numbers in aviation.

q: 10. Beaufort scale measure velocity of wind at a height of
explain: Standard meteorological wind speed measurements are taken at a height of 10 meters above the ground.

q: 11. For class A airport, the difference of RL of higher and lower edges of the conical surface is
explain: For Class A airports, the conical surface extends to a vertical height of 100 meters above the inner horizontal surface.

q: 12. The length of runway is increased per 300 m rise above M.S.I ...........
explain: ICAO recommends a 7% increase in runway length for every 300 meters (approx 1000 ft) of elevation above Mean Sea Level.

q: 13. The reduced level of the proposed site of an air port is 2500 m above M.S.L. If the recommended length by I.C.A.O. for the runway at sea level is 2500 m, the required length of the runway is ...........
explain: Correction for elevation: $2500 + (2500/300) \times 0.07 \times 2500 \approx 3958$. The key indicates 'b' (3725), likely using a different coefficient or rounding method.

q: 14. Effective length of a runway is the distance between
options: the points of intersection of the obstruction line and the runway centre line
explain: Effective length accounts for the distance required to clear obstacles along the flight path according to safety slopes.

q: 15. *According to I.C.A.O., recommended length of airport is decided on
explain: The basic runway length must be corrected for elevation, site temperature, and longitudinal gradient.

q: 16. Total correction for elevation, temperature and gradient for a runway should not be more than ...........
explain: ICAO suggests that if the total correction for elevation, temperature, and gradient exceeds 35%, a specific site study should be conducted.

q: 17. *The height of the pilot's eye above runway surface is assumed
explain: For design purposes, specifically sight distance and gradient changes, the pilot's eye height is assumed to be 3m.

q: 18. The capacity of parallel runway pattern depends upon ...........
options: weather conditions and navigational aids available
lateral spacing between two runways and weather conditions
lateral spacing between two runways and navigational aids available
lateral spacing between two runways, weather conditions and navigational aids available
explain: Parallel runway capacity is a complex function of how far apart they are (for simultaneous use), the weather (VFR vs IFR), and the precision of the radar/navigation aids.

q: 19. The length of runway under standard conditions is 2500 m. The elevation of airport site is 300 m. Its reference temperature is 33.05°C. If the runway is to be constructed with an effective gradient of 0.25 percent, the corrected runway length will be ............
explain: Corrections are applied sequentially: 1. Elevation (7% per 300m), 2. Temperature (1% per 1°C rise above standard), 3. Gradient (20% per 1% effective gradient). Total calculation leads to 2800m.

q: 20. For determining the basic runway length, the landing case requires that aircraft should come to a stop within p% of the landing distance. The value of p is ............
explain: Safety regulations require that the aircraft must be able to land and stop within 60% of the available runway length.

q: 21. Runway threshold is indicated by a series of parallel lines starting from a distance of ............
explain: Threshold stripes start 6 meters from the beginning of the runway to indicate the start of the landing area.

q: 22. *The bearing of the 1st end of straight runway is 90°. Find the runway number of 1st end
explain: The runway number is 90/10 = 9.

q: 23. For supersonic transport aircraft, the minimum turning radius of taxiway is ............
explain: Supersonic aircraft have longer wheelbases and higher speeds, requiring a larger turning radius of 180m.

q: 24. The National pride project concerned with airport is
explain: Nijgadh International Airport is a designated National Pride Project of Nepal.

q: 25. As the elevation of airport increases the runway length
explain: Higher elevation means thinner air, which reduces lift, requiring a longer runway for takeoff.

q: 26. As the elevation & temperature of airport increases the density of air
explain: Both increasing altitude and increasing temperature lead to lower air density.

q: 27. Runway dimension of TIA after extension held in 2020 AD is
explain: The runway was extended to 3350 meters to accommodate larger wide-body aircraft.

q: 28. Runway surface strength of TIA is
explain: This refers to the Pavement Classification Number (PCN) value for the TIA runway.

q: 29. *ACN refers to
explain: ACN (Aircraft Classification Number) expresses the relative effect of an aircraft on a pavement.

q: 30. The old name of TIA was
explain: It was originally known as Gauchar Airport before being renamed Tribhuvan International Airport.

q: 31. Flight time refers to ............
options: time taken between departure time (first move) to arrival time (to rest at the end of flight) of an aircraft
explain: Flight time is defined as the total time from the moment an aircraft first moves under its own power for the purpose of taking off until the moment it comes to rest at the end of the flight.

q: 32. The runway orientation is made so that landing and takeoff are ............
explain: Landing and takeoff are performed against the wind (headwind) to reduce the ground speed required to achieve lift or to stop.

q: 33. *Runway is designed on the basis of
explain: Design loads and geometry for runways are heavily influenced by aircraft gear configuration (nose gear/main gear).

q: 34. The metrological condition which influences the size and location of an airport is
explain: Meteorological factors like wind direction and pressure (altitude) determine orientation and runway length.

q: 35. *Classification of Airport by ICAO is based on
explain: ICAO airport classification uses a code based on both runway length and aircraft dimensions.

q: 36. The headquarter of International Civil Aviation Organization (I.C.A.O.) is located in ............
explain: ICAO is headquartered in Montreal, Quebec, Canada.

q: 37. *For A,B and C types of airports, longitudinal gradient of the runway recommended by ICAO is :
explain: ICAO recommends a maximum longitudinal gradient of 1.5% for major airport categories (A, B, C).

q: 38. *In FY 2072/73, various accidents were occured and there was a heavy losses of lives in Nepal. Among the various airports which of the following is most dangerous in Nepal.
explain: Tenzing-Hillary (Lukla) Airport is considered one of the most dangerous due to terrain and short runway.

q: 39. *A domestic airport is an airport that handles only
explain: Domestic airports serve only internal flights within the same country.

q: 40. According to the I.C.A.O. the strength of runway pavements, have been coded by ............
explain: The ACN-PCN system (or LCN) uses numeric values and code letters for strength. Answer key marks 'd'.

q: 41. Two single runway may be arranged so as to have ............
explain: Multiple runways can be oriented in parallel, intersecting (X), or diverging (L/T) patterns depending on wind rose requirements.

q: 42. The marking of taxiway is yellow while on apron is ............
explain: Both taxiway and apron markings (lead-in lines, parking positions) are generally yellow.

q: 43. The best direction of a runway is along the direction of ............
options: longest line on wind rose diagram
shortest line on wind rose diagram
line clear of wind rose diagram
explain: The longest line (spoke) on a wind rose diagram indicates the direction of prevailing winds, which is the ideal orientation for a runway.
